responsibilities: Design and operate the end-to-end gameplay analytics ecosystem.
Define tracking, storage, processing, and reporting architecture.
Own data correctness and make judgement calls when quality checks flag anomalies.
Build the semantic layer that translates raw gameplay data into validated gameplay and business concepts.
Develop AI-driven automated reporting, dashboards, and insight-generation workflows.
Evaluate and implement AI tools, agents, and workflows that improve analytics speed, reliability, and depth.
Review AI-generated code and analytics on critical paths before they reach production.
Identify opportunities, risks, anomalies, and trends across gameplay and player behavior.
Support product, balancing, design, and leadership teams with data-driven recommendations.
Translate complex datasets into clear, actionable insights.
Help define how the wider engineering organization adopts agentic practices.
Establish standards for tooling, review processes, quality gates, and what "done" means when agents generate most of the implementation.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: you'll use agents to dramatically increase your throughput while remaining the architect, reviewer, and final owner of correctness
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Speed phrases ('dramatically increase your throughput', 'build something new at high speed') sit alongside heavy correctness, review-gate and verification language.
evidence.domain_risk: build the analytics foundation from the first tracked event to the first board-level KPI
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Mobile game analytics feeding product and monetisation decisions, with no regulatory or financial reporting language.
evidence.data_team_maturity: there is no data warehouse yet
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The role chooses the stack and builds the first warehouse for a new game, so the data function does not yet exist.
evidence.jd_authorship: Own data correctness and make judgement calls when quality checks flag anomalies.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Bullets name concrete gameplay analytics, semantic layer and agentic review work, and the interview section describes the actual workflow expected.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Support product, balancing, design, and leadership teams with data-driven recommendations.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience is game product, balancing and design teams working on gameplay and player behaviour.
evidence.autonomy_level: You will choose the stack, set it up, and build the analytics foundation
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role defines the architecture and the organisation's agentic standards ('Define tracking, storage, processing, and reporting architecture').
evidence.ai_role: Develop AI-driven automated reporting, dashboards, and insight-generation workflows.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate both uses coding agents daily and builds the semantic layer and AI-powered analytics tools that run on it; the tie-breaker places both signals in ai_enabler.
evidence.testing_framing: Own data correctness and make judgement calls when quality checks flag anomalies.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data correctness and quality gates are framed as the candidate's own responsibility.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: which fall apart when real decisions depend on the numbers
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The fear is unreviewed AI output producing wrong numbers, framed as an engineering risk secondary to building the foundation.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role builds the analytics stack for a new game from scratch.
evidence.loss_aversion: Review AI-generated code and analytics on critical paths before they reach production.
